title: K-th Smallest Gap Among All Pairs
statement:
You get an integer array nums. For every pair of positions i < j, its gap is |nums[i] − nums[j]|. There are n · (n − 1) / 2 gaps, and equal gaps from different pairs are all counted.

Sort all the gaps in increasing order and return the k-th one (1-indexed).

examples.why: The gaps are 3 (4−1), 3 (7−4) and 6 (7−1). Sorted: 3, 3, 6. The second is 3, because duplicates count separately.
Two pairs have gap 0, the other four have gap 7.
k is the number of pairs, so the answer is the largest gap: max − min.

hints: Listing all gaps costs O(n²) memory and time. Can you instead answer "how many gaps are at most d?" quickly?
Sort the array. For a fixed d, as the right index moves right, the leftmost index within distance d never moves left. Two pointers count the pairs in O(n).
The count is monotone in d. Binary search for the smallest d whose count is at least k.

explain.intuition:
The answer is some value between 0 and max − min. For any candidate d, the number of pairs with gap ≤ d only grows as d grows. The k-th smallest gap is the smallest d for which that count reaches k. So binary search on d instead of on positions.

Counting is fast after sorting: for each right end j, slide i forward while nums[j] − nums[i] > d. Every index from i to j − 1 pairs with j, so add j − i. The left pointer only moves forward, so a count costs O(n).
steps: While lo < hi, let mid = ⌊(lo + hi) / 2⌋ and count pairs with gap ≤ mid using two pointers.
If the count is at least k, set hi = mid; otherwise lo = mid + 1.
Return lo. It is a real gap, because the count jumps exactly at real gap values.
pitfalls: Counting distinct gaps instead of pairs, which breaks the first example.
Searching for a d where the count equals k exactly. With duplicates, the count may jump past k.
Resetting the left pointer for every right end, which makes each count O(n²).

complexity.time: O(n log n + n log W), W = max − min

solutions.title: List and sort every gap
solutions.idea: Generate all n · (n − 1) / 2 gaps, sort them, and index.

solutions.title: Binary search on the gap with two-pointer counting
solutions.idea: Find the smallest d such that at least k pairs have gap ≤ d.
solutions.time: O(n log n + n log W)

followups: Values are small (≤ 1000) but n is huge. Can a counting array replace the binary search?
Find the k-th smallest pair sum instead. Does the same approach work?
